definitions.gloss: to go, to move (toward a destination)
definitions.explanation: Expresses movement away from the speaker's current location toward a destination. The opposite of {来|く}る (to come). Used when the speaker is not at the destination.
When attached to the te-form of another verb (〜ていく), indicates an action continuing into the future or moving away from the speaker's perspective.

examples.japanese: {一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}きましょう。
{明日|あした}、{東京|とうきょう}に{行|い}く。
{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}かない?
{毎年|まいとし}{夏|なつ}になると、{家族|かぞく}で{海|うみ}に{行|い}く。{子供|こども}たちはいつも{楽|たの}しみにしている。
examples.english: Every summer, our family goes to the beach. The kids always look forward to it.

examples.japanese: {どんどん|どんどん}{増|ふ}えていく。
これから{勉強|べんきょう}していく。
examples.english: I will continue to study from now on.

examples.japanese: {少|すこ}しずつ{分|わ}かっていく。
これからも{頑張|がんば}っていきたい。
examples.english: I want to keep doing my best from now on.

examples.japanese: {時代|じだい}が{変|か}わっていく{中|なか}で、{私|わたし}たちも{新|あたら}しいことを{学|まな}んでいかなければならない。
examples.english: As times change, we too must continue learning new things.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Counterpart: {来|く}る (to come). Pattern: Xに/へ{行|い}く (go to X).

ASPECT: ている indicates ongoing action or resulting state. {行|い}っている can mean 'is going' or 'has gone (and is there now).'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{学校|がっこう}に{行|い}く (go to school)
・{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}く (go shopping)
・{遊|あそ}びに{行|い}く (go to hang out)
・〜て{行|い}く (go and do ~, or do ~ as one goes)

IRREGULAR FORMS:
・Te-form: {行|い}って (not {行|い}いて)
・Also read as ゆく in literary contexts

The auxiliary 〜ていく indicates continuing into the future or moving away.
